title: Palworld Best Mining Pals | Aegidron, Astegon, Anubis and Early Picks | Palworld Guide
description: Palworld 1.0 mining Pals explained: Aegidron, Astegon, Blazamut, Knocklem, Anubis, plus the early picks Tombat, Penking, Dumud, Cattiva and Depresso. Checked against Pindrop and PalMods in November 2026.
joke: A good mining Pal never asks for a coffee break, which is more than I can say about me during a long base build.

sections.heading: Intro
sections.script: Stone, ore, coal, sulfur and quartz decide how fast your base grows. If your mining is slow, your smelting and crafting stall, and nothing feels worse. In this guide we look at the best mining Pals in Palworld 1.0, from the cheap workers you can catch early to the late game specialists that sit at the top of the ranking. The numbers come from two independent sites, Pindrop and PalMods, checked in November 2026, and when they disagree we speak loosely or leave it out. Only Palworld 1.0 information is used here, because mining levels were rebalanced in this update and older guides are now out of date. You will hear which Pals lead, which are the best early picks and how to set up your base so mining never stops. Stay until the end for a simple plan.

sections.heading: What changed in 1.0
sections.script: The first thing to know is that old rankings no longer apply. Palworld 1.0 rebalanced work suitability, so the old one to four feeling is gone, and the top miners now reach level eight. Both sites we checked use the same idea. A Pal has a mining level, a higher level means it can work harder nodes, and the ranking is built on that number. Some Pals can mine only at level one, and a few can reach seven or eight. The practical rule is simple. A Pal needs a high enough mining level for the node it is sent to, and a Pal with a higher level is the safer choice for tougher resources. Pindrop counts fifty seven Pals that can mine in total, and its guide narrows that to the twenty two worth carrying. Many guides that call themselves 1.0 still use old tiers, so always check the date.

sections.heading: Aegidron at the top
sections.script: At the very top of the list is Aegidron. Both Pindrop and PalMods give Aegidron mining level eight, the only Pal that goes higher than seven. PalMods ranks it first in its mining table and calls it the current leader. If you can field an Aegidron, it is the best natural miner in the game. The catch is that it is a late game Pal, so most players will not have one early. Treat it as the goal, not the starting point. Think of it like a long term project. You catch cheap workers now, build up your base, then replace them one by one as your roster grows. That way your mining never stops while you chase the big names. It also saves you from wasting rare catches on jobs a cheaper Pal could do. Aegidron also shows why the new level scale matters, because the gap between a level seven and a level eight worker is the gap between good and best. A single level difference between your miner and the node can decide whether the job is done at all, so the top specialists are worth the effort once you reach the end of your journey.

sections.heading: The level seven group
sections.script: Right below Aegidron is a strong group at mining level seven. Both sites list Astegon, Blazamut, Blazamut Ryu, Knocklem and Knocklem Ignis at that level. Astegon is a Dragon and Dark Pal and Pindrop calls it the strongest practical miner you can actually catch, because it shares the top with Blazamut and the Knocklem line. Blazamut is the fire alternative, the Fire type answer to Astegon. If you prefer one that suits your theme, you can pick whichever you can get first. All of them are late game, so they usually come after the World Tree and the big boss fights. If you have any of these in your box, send it to your mining station and let it work. Note that Pindrop lists the Knocklem and Blazamut Ryu versions at the same level as the originals, so if you own a variant, it is just as good at the job. That makes the level seven group wider than most players expect, and it gives you several ways to reach the same result.

sections.heading: Anubis the mid game star
sections.script: For most players, the most important miner is Anubis. Both sites list Anubis at mining level six, and Pindrop calls it the mid game miner most players reach first. It also helps outside mining. Pindrop says Anubis also has a high handiwork level, so one Pal can craft as well as mine. That is great for a small base, where you do not have room for a separate worker on every job. Anubis is a Ground Pal and a classic base worker for good reason, since it is rare to find a Pal that does so much at once. If you do not own a level seven Pal yet, Anubis is the one to build your mining plan around, and it will carry you through most of the game.

sections.heading: Early game miners
sections.script: Now the budget picks. Do not wait for the late game to start mining. PalMods lists a shortlist of workers you can catch before level twenty. Tombat mines at level three and can be found from around level twelve, Penking also mines at level three and shows up from around level twenty. Dumud mines at level two, and Cattiva and Depresso both mine at level one. Cattiva is easy to find, since it lives in the starting area. Depresso can be caught from around level four. Both sites give the same mining level for each of these. Put Cattiva or Depresso on stone, and move up to Dumud, Tombat or Penking when you need ore. These are not fast workers, but they get your first furnace going. They are also cheap, so you can catch several and let them share the load while you work towards something better. Many players overlook that a handful of low level miners, together, can keep a young base supplied long before the first big specialist arrives.

sections.heading: Match the Pal to the resource
sections.script: A mining Pal does not need to be the best in the game, it just needs to clear the node. Both sites explain that nodes need a minimum mining level, and the cheapest way to progress is to match the Pal to the resource. Stone needs the lowest level, so a level one Pal is enough. Ore needs a bit more, so move to a level two or three Pal. Coal, sulfur and quartz sit higher still, so bring your strongest miner. Pindrop even has a table of the best Pal for each resource. If a Pal stands next to a rock and does nothing, it is probably below the level that node needs, so swap it for a stronger one. Speed matters too, but the level requirement comes first.

sections.heading: Set up your base
sections.script: A few base tips make any mining team better. Build your base close to the ore, because walking time wastes work time. Use more than one mining Pal if you can, so the line of crafting never waits for stone. Pindrop also points out that some miners double as other workers. Anubis can craft, so a good miner can fill two jobs. After you reach the late game, swap in your Astegon, Blazamut or Aegidron, and move the early workers to lighter jobs. Check your work panel often, because it shows which Pal is doing what and whether anyone is stuck without the right level.

sections.heading: Your plan
sections.script: Here is the plan in one breath. Start with Cattiva or Depresso on stone, add Dumud, Tombat or Penking for ore, aim for Anubis as your mid game miner, and finish with Astegon, Blazamut or the mighty Aegidron. Keep an eye on the mining level, because it decides what each Pal can actually do. Remember that this list is for Palworld 1.0, and that every number comes from two sites that agree. Which Pal is mining for you right now, and which one are you hunting next? Tell us in the comments, and subscribe to HarryBeast Gaming for more Palworld guides every day.
